seoTitle: Franchise broker duties: claims, FDD delivery and records

sections.heading: A broker agreement does not transfer every legal duty
paragraphs: The federal definition of franchise seller is broad: it can include the brand’s people and outside brokers involved in selling. The rule restricts specified seller conduct, while responsibility for furnishing the FDD rests with the franchisor. Those are related but different responsibilities.

The brand therefore needs more than a referral contract stating that the broker “handles compliance.” Identify who speaks to prospects, whose offering is sold, who approves materials and who controls formal disclosure. The actual sales activity matters, including introductions that contain substantive claims.

sections.heading: Control spoken and private messages too
paragraphs: Review presentations, webinars, broker portals, private messages and conversations about likely sales or profit. Sellers must not contradict required disclosures or misrepresent a reference as independent. Performance claims need the applicable reasonable basis, written supporting evidence and disclosure treatment.

A broker’s personal spreadsheet or informal answer can create the same review question as a polished recruitment slide. Give sellers approved materials and a named contact for questions they cannot answer from them. Preserve the version actually used, not just the current master file.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the predictable-margin introduction
paragraphs: A broker introduces a cleaning brand to a “territory investor” and says an employed local manager can produce a predictable margin. The expansion lead does not assume that calling it an introduction removes the sales claim.

The team preserves the exact statement, pauses its reuse and compares it with the relevant Item 19 treatment and supporting material. It also checks which FDD was supplied and by whom. The issue is not solved by renaming the candidate an investor. This example identifies a review task; it does not find that a particular transaction violated the rule.

The filled record separates the broker’s statement from the franchisor’s document-delivery job. Giving one employee both tasks can be an internal arrangement; it does not turn a referral contract into a transfer of every legal duty. The claims-review assignment is an optional internal business role, not a newly prescribed legal office.

The franchisor’s disclosure owner checks the document, recipient and timetable separately.

sections.heading: Make a seller-responsibility sheet
paragraphs: Use the sheet as a business control supporting the actual duties. It is not a state authorisation to sell.
bullets: Name every speaker, contracting entity, channel, payment arrangement and permitted territory.
Identify who approves materials and who answers earnings questions.
Assign current-FDD delivery, receipt records and timetable checks to named people.
Keep the actual communications and document versions with the prospect’s file.
Check separate state broker, advertising, registration and sales requirements before relying on the process.

seoTitle: Franchise recruitment ads: check earnings claims and context

sections.heading: Compare the actual advertisement with the disclosure
paragraphs: Franchise sellers must not make claims that contradict required disclosures. Financial performance representations must also satisfy the applicable basis, written-support and disclosure conditions. Not every brand message is a performance representation; assess what this message communicates.

An earnings or sales figure should be checked against Item 19 and the actual supporting material. A promising result from the home market does not alone justify the U.S. claim. A disclaimer or broker label does not cure a contradiction with required disclosure.

sections.heading: Keep the context with the number
paragraphs: Save the image, caption, landing page and spoken presentation together. Distinguish revenue from profit, identify included and excluded units, and record geography, period and operating model. Those facts help explain what a number does and does not show.

Review testimonials and any incentive given to a reference, including a claim that the reference is independent. When source information changes, find every live advertisement using it rather than correcting one slide while an older version remains on a broker portal.

sections.heading: Fictional example: turning a past margin into a target
paragraphs: A technical-services brand has one home-country unit with a 20% operating margin. Its U.S. recruitment deck says “target 20%.” Finance initially regards the word target as enough explanation.

The review instead asks what a prospective partner would understand, whether there is a reasonable basis for the U.S. statement, which costs and units the result includes, and how the claim is disclosed. Calling an achieved figure a target does not answer those questions. The team pauses or revises the slide according to the review rather than treating this fictional number as an approved forecast.

The useful decision is not simply whether 20% is arithmetically correct. It is whether this complete message, for this audience, has the necessary basis and treatment. An optional internal claim register can record revise or pause while the missing facts are resolved; it does not itself approve the advertisement.

That result alone does not establish a U.S. operator’s likely margin.

The U.S. deck changes the description to target 20%.
The word target does not supply a reasonable basis, written support or the required disclosure treatment.
Missing context
The reviewer asks about costs, units, period and operating model.
An accurate percentage can still leave the prospect with an unsupported impression.
Live versions
The slide may also appear on a landing page or broker portal.
Changing the master slide does not establish that every old version was withdrawn.

sections.heading: Record a decision for each usable version
paragraphs: The claim register is an optional management tool supporting the legal requirements. Record approve, revise or pause, the responsible person and the remaining evidence needed.
bullets: Write each quantitative or implied performance statement exactly.
Link it to the corresponding disclosure and written support.
Keep context, exclusions, period and sample information visible.
Track every approved channel and withdraw superseded versions.
Check state advertising filings, required wording and sales requirements separately before publication.

seoTitle: Business Opportunity Rule: customer promises and disclosure

sections.heading: The purchaser’s business can be new even if the seller is old
paragraphs: Part 437’s new-business question concerns the prospective purchaser. The seller’s long operating history does not remove that issue. The definition also requires payment and specified representations that the seller or a designated person will provide locations, customers/accounts, or buy back what the purchaser produces.

Examine the represented arrangement as a whole. It is not enough to identify a fee without the other conditions, or a new activity without the specified promise. Existing companies may need to assess whether the proposed activity is a new line or business for the purchaser.

sections.heading: Providing customers differs from teaching marketing
paragraphs: The definition can reach recommended lead-generation or locator services, customer lists and some payment-collection arrangements. General business-development advice, training and advertising alone are not treated as providing customers under that definition.

Preserve the exact promise, including what a designated third party will do. “Marketing support” is too vague if it could mean either a general sales course or a promise of named paying accounts. Those are different factual questions.

sections.heading: Keep its disclosure and record duties separate
paragraphs: For an arrangement within Part 437, § 437.2 requires the prescribed written disclosure and applicable earnings information at least seven calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or payment/other consideration. Section 437.7 separately requires specified disclosure versions, receipts, contracts and earnings support to be retained for three years.

The existing review records an unresolved interaction: § 437.8 literally uses $500 while cross-referencing the minimum-payment franchise exemption in§ 436.8(a)(1), whose current amount differs. Do not silently update one text, treat $500 as the current Franchise Rule threshold, or conclude an exemption from that cross-reference. The interaction remains an assigned scope question.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a new cleaning line with named accounts
paragraphs: A facilities brand sells an established local operator a new cleaning line, required software and a promise of named customer accounts. The buyer’s existing business does not alone decide whether the new-business condition is met.

The team records the purchaser’s current and proposed activities, payment schedule and exact accounts promise. It asks for the Part 437/franchise classification and cross-reference questions to be resolved before accepting money, then applies the appropriate disclosure process. Relevant state business-opportunity and franchise rules remain independent.

The difference is the actual promise, not which version sounds more like ordinary support. If Part 437 applies, its seven-calendar-day disclosure and three-year specified-record duties are separate from any independently applicable franchise and state requirements.

This changes the represented assistance. Assess it together with the purchaser’s new-business facts and required payment.

Review the purchaser’s new-business activity, required payment and exact seller or designated-person promise together. Part 437 has its own disclosure and record duties, while its payment-exemption cross-reference remains unresolved in this review. The seller’s long history does not decide the purchaser’s situation or supply an exemption.

seoTitle: U.S. company formation versus foreign qualification by state

sections.heading: The same entity can be domestic in one state and foreign in another
paragraphs: A company formed in one U.S. state can be foreign for qualification purposes in another. This use of foreign is separate from the owner’s nationality or the presence of an overseas parent. Keep those meanings distinct in the expansion file.

The Small Business Administration describes possible certificates of authority and, in many states, evidence of good standing. Its overview directs readers to individual state offices for requirements and fees. It does not establish one nationwide activity threshold or an automatic registration rule for every customer.

sections.heading: Describe each entity’s actual work in the additional state
paragraphs: Record employees and their work locations, premises, customer service and contract performance. Identify which company signs the customer contract and which employs the team. The relevant state office or reviewer can then apply its actual statutory test.

Do not turn a national website, one customer or an owner’s address into a universal qualification answer. Those facts may be relevant, but the conclusion belongs to the particular state rule. Formation, qualification, tax accounts, franchise sales, sector licences and premises approval remain different questions.

sections.heading: Fictional example: Delaware formation and a Texas depot
paragraphs: A Singapore-owned business forms a Delaware LLC and plans a staffed service depot in Texas. The Delaware record proves that the entity was created there. It does not determine Texas qualification, payroll accounts, customer-site licences or the depot’s occupancy conditions.

The expansion lead prepares a Texas activity file showing the depot, employees and contract work. The team obtains a dated qualification decision from the appropriate authority or reviewer and tracks the other requirements separately. This is not a recommendation to incorporate again or a finding that a particular Texas filing is required.

This row does not tell the company to incorporate again or declare a particular Texas filing due. It gives the reviewer a named entity and concrete activities to assess. Keep the resulting qualification decision beside, rather than in place of, the separate payroll and premises decisions.

Formation record identifies the company and its legal home.
It does not decide the additional-state operating requirements.

The plan includes premises, employees and service work.
Apply the actual Texas qualification test and exceptions to those activities.

The same depot will employ people and occupy premises.
Tax accounts, customer-site licences and occupancy are separate from qualification.

sections.heading: Maintain one operating-entity register
paragraphs: Use the register to connect the company’s activities with the authorities and decisions relevant to them.

Add each additional state and the activities performed there.
Record the applicable authority, reviewed requirement and filing decision.
Keep tax accounts and sector/local permits in separate columns.
Assign registered-agent and annual-report responsibilities where applicable.
Leave unanswered qualification questions explicit, with an owner and next action.

seoTitle: LLC federal tax classification and Form 8832 elections

sections.heading: Separate legal form, tax treatment and immigration
paragraphs: State company law, federal tax classification and the owner’s immigration position answer different questions. For a domestic eligible entity, two or more members generally mean default partnership treatment; one owner generally means disregarded treatment unless an election applies.

Foreign-entity defaults differ and depend in part on limited liability. Do not copy the U.S. subsidiary’s default onto the overseas parent. A tax reviewer needs each entity’s actual characteristics and ownership rather than a group-wide assumption.

sections.heading: An election has limits and a procedure
paragraphs: An eligible-entity election follows a defined procedure. Its ordinary effective date can be up to 75 days before filing or up to 12 months after filing. A change election generally has a 60-month restriction, subject to exceptions; an initial election effective on formation is treated differently. The procedure is set out in § 301.7701-3 and the Form 8832 instructions.

Late relief has conditions and should not be assumed. The retrieved Form 8832 is revision December 2013, not a new 2026 form. Use the applicable instructions and actual dates rather than treating an old revision date as evidence that a different deadline applies.

sections.heading: Fictional example: one member, but reporting still needs review
paragraphs: An overseas company forms a one-member domestic LLC. The CFO understands the possible disregarded treatment but mistakenly concludes that no U.S. information return can be needed.

The preparer separates the classification from foreign-owner reporting, including the Form 5472 and related pro forma return questions for reportable transactions. The team records ownership, funding and other transactions alongside any election proposal. The example does not choose the entity’s treatment or conclude which return is due; it shows why one label cannot close every tax question.

Self-check: if a desired effective date is outside the ordinary window, does writing that date on the form establish that it applies? No. Conditional relief and the actual election procedure still need assessment. An internal tax calendar helps organise the facts; it does not choose or validate the election.

Finance records the intended effective date and actual filing date separately.
Check the ordinary window: up to 75 days before filing or 12 months after filing.

The file identifies any previous election and when it applied.
Check the general 60-month change restriction, initial-formation treatment and any relevant exception.
Reporting
The owner supplies funding and transaction records.
Disregarded treatment does not answer the separate Form 5472 and pro forma return questions.

sections.heading: Prepare an entity-classification brief
paragraphs: Finance should supply the dates and records; the tax reviewer decides the applicable default, valid election and affected returns.
bullets: Identify the exact entity, formation jurisdiction, owners and liability characteristics.
State the default treatment and intended treatment separately.
Record the proposed effective date, filing date and tax identification number.
Check eligibility, change restrictions, any exception and conditional late relief.
List related information-return, state-tax, treaty and immigration questions without assuming a favourable result.

seoTitle: Transfer pricing for parent royalties and support services

sections.heading: Separate the transactions hidden inside one invoice
paragraphs: A parent may license a brand, provide remote support, lend working capital and supply products. Those activities have different facts even if the group issues one invoice. Start by describing what is actually supplied, who benefits and what each entity does.

The arm’s-length rule compares results with dealings between unrelated taxpayers in comparable circumstances. Saying “our royalty is 6%” states a policy, not the evidence needed to show that the controlled arrangement meets that standard (§ 1.482-1).

sections.heading: Build the factual comparison before selecting a method
paragraphs: The best-method rule seeks the most reliable measure under the facts and circumstances. Reliability depends on comparability, data quality and assumptions. An unrelated franchisee’s rate cannot simply be copied without considering differences in rights, services and business circumstances.

Document who develops, owns, funds and maintains intellectual property. For support services, identify deliverables, staff time, costs and beneficiaries. Explain each entity’s functions, assets and risks in ordinary business terms: what it does, what it uses and which business consequences it bears.

sections.heading: Fictional example: one royalty bundles several jobs
paragraphs: A European parent invoices its new U.S. subsidiary a single royalty for the name, initial training and quarterly technical support. The finance lead first separates the rights and services, identifies the staff delivering them and records the subsidiary’s own sales and support functions.

That file allows the reviewer to ask which pricing methods and comparisons are appropriate. It does not assume that every cost is chargeable, every service belongs in one transaction or a third-party franchise rate applies without adjustment. The price must follow the relevant analysis, not the other way round.

The table separates business facts before a method is selected. It does not conclude that each activity must be priced separately or that every cost may be charged. Withholding asks what tax the payer must deduct; that is a different question from whether the controlled price meets the applicable standard.

The package label does not establish a reliable comparable, pricing method or final rate.

sections.heading: Keep a pricing file distinct from withholding compliance
paragraphs: Record the agreement, actual conduct, data sources, method question, cost allocations, assumptions, invoices and currency. Explain differences between the written contract and what the teams actually do.

This review covers § 1.482-1(a)–(c), not every method for services or intangibles, documentation rule or penalty defence. Withholding, treaties and foreign-country transfer-pricing requirements remain separate. A sound starting file makes those reviews possible; it does not establish the final rate.

seoTitle: U.S. business visits: meetings versus operating work

sections.heading: Use the permitted examples without stretching them
paragraphs: The State Department lists consulting with business associates, attending relevant conferences and negotiating contracts among business examples. It separately lists employment among activities not permitted on visitor visas.

Those examples are not an individual eligibility or admission decision. Owning the U.S. company or receiving pay overseas does not alone settle whether the planned activity is permitted. Describe the work instead of relying on the job title or source of payment.

sections.heading: Replace “launch support” with a real itinerary
paragraphs: Write what will happen each day, who benefits, who performs the task, where it takes place and how the traveller is paid. Launch support might mean investor meetings, interviews, staff training, ordinary management or servicing a customer. Those activities should not be treated as interchangeable.

Identify the host, customer sites, duration and pattern of repeat visits. Separate negotiation and observation from hands-on delivery or ordinary management work. Where training, installation or service activity is borderline, ask the exact question rather than assuming the general meeting examples answer it.

sections.heading: Fictional example: negotiations followed by repairs
paragraphs: A technical founder proposes three days negotiating a distribution contract and then two weeks repairing customer equipment beside the new U.S. team. The permitted meeting examples do not establish permission for the repair work.

The trip owner splits the itinerary into its actual activities and obtains an activity-specific answer before relying on the operational portion. If that work requires a different staffing plan, the commercial timetable needs to reflect it. This example does not decide whether any particular alternative visa or work category is available.

The same person and trip can contain different activities. Describe and assess each one before the customer timetable depends on it. Moving the repair work under a heading such as launch support does not make it the same activity as negotiating a contract.

Negotiate a distribution contract.
Negotiating contracts is among the listed visitor examples; the individual’s eligibility and admission remain separate.

Repair customer equipment beside the U.S. team.
The negotiation example does not establish permission for this hands-on work.
Payment and ownership facts
Record who pays the founder and the company relationship.
Overseas pay or ownership alone does not settle the activity’s treatment.

sections.heading: Give the trip and the staffing plan separate decisions
paragraphs: Keep a visit-activity brief with the relevant purpose evidence and unresolved questions. Record who will review them before bookings or customer commitments depend on the traveller’s presence.

A visa does not guarantee admission; entry is decided by the admitting authorities. Any L-1, E-2 or other work-authorised staffing proposal needs its own assessment. Do not use this general visitor guide to conclude a person’s visa, ESTA, productive-training or hands-on-service position.

seoTitle: Federal overtime: coverage, workweeks and staffing cost

sections.heading: A small business can still need a coverage assessment
paragraphs: Department of Labor Fact Sheet 14 distinguishes enterprise coverage from individual coverage. The ordinary enterprise test includes at least two employees and at least $500,000 in annual business volume; specified institutions have different coverage treatment.

Individual interstate-commerce coverage can apply even when the enterprise does not meet that volume. A modest launch budget is therefore not a conclusion that wage law does not apply. Establish the employer, work and relevant coverage facts before treating a threshold as a general escape.

sections.heading: Calculate overtime by the fixed workweek
paragraphs: For covered nonexempt employees, the federal baseline is generally at least one and one-half the regular rate for hours over 40 in a fixed workweek. Hours cannot be averaged between a busy and a quiet week.

Paying a salary does not by itself establish an overtime exemption, and an advance-approval policy does not waive overtime already earned. This guide does not supply a current salary-exemption threshold or decide who is exempt. Actual duties, compensation and the applicable current rules need their own assessment.

sections.heading: Fictional example: 45 hours one week, 35 the next
paragraphs: Assume a covered nonexempt technician works 45 hours at a $20 regular hourly rate, with no other compensation affecting that rate. Straight-time pay for 45 hours is $900. The additional half-time premium for the five overtime hours is $50, producing $950 before employer costs.

If the technician works 35 hours the following week, that does not erase the first week’s overtime by making a two-week average of 40 hours. The example is arithmetic on stated assumptions, not a local wage quotation or complete regular-rate calculation. Bonuses or other compensation can require additional analysis.

The illustration assumes a covered nonexempt worker and no other compensation affecting the $20 regular rate. Counting $900 and then adding another full $30 for each overtime hour would count the straight-time component twice. Coverage, exemption status, bonuses and other employer costs remain separate questions.

sections.heading: Prepare the staffing record before fixing prices
paragraphs: The local employer should assign timekeeping and payroll responsibilities, with facts that permit the coverage and exemption questions to be answered.

Budget hours by workweek, including expected busy periods.
List all compensation components for regular-rate review.
Keep salary/exemption, contractor status and joint-employer questions separate.
Add state/local wage, leave, tax-account and other employer costs rather than treating federal overtime as the whole payroll budget.

seoTitle: First-job safety: employer duties at customer premises

sections.heading: A safety clause is not the safety system
paragraphs: OSH Act§ 5(a) requires each covered employer to provide a workplace free of recognised hazards causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm and to comply with applicable occupational safety and health standards. The actual employer and work facts matter.

A clause saying the operator handles safety does not show that hazards have been assessed, equipment supplied or workers trained. Nor does the brand’s location abroad by itself decide legal responsibility. Identify actual control and employment facts before drawing that conclusion.

sections.heading: Separate law, customer requirements and brand standards
paragraphs: Applicable law, a customer’s site rules and the brand’s operating requirements may overlap, but they are different records. The OSHA overview covers safe workplaces, applicable standards, hazard information and training. A customer’s insurance certificate or induction card does not demonstrate that all applicable standards have been met.

List chemicals, equipment, access conditions and foreseeable task hazards. Identify the federal OSHA or state-plan authority and the task-specific standards needing review. Assign who supplies equipment, conducts training, authorises work and responds when conditions change.

sections.heading: Fictional example: remote training and powered equipment
paragraphs: A foreign facilities brand trains a U.S. partner remotely. The partner’s employees will use powered equipment at a customer site. The operating lead gathers the actual equipment information, site conditions, training records and work-authorisation process.

That record reveals which training or equipment evidence is missing and who must resolve it before the job depends on readiness. It also identifies questions about each entity’s control. The example does not determine joint-employer status or decide that a remote course satisfies a task-specific standard.

This is an optional preparation card, not a safety certification. Its purpose is to reveal the missing standard, equipment or training evidence before the job relies on readiness. The guide’s unverified task-specific and state-plan questions must remain open until answered; the card itself does not decide joint-employer status.

paragraphs: As practical preparation, bring the employer/site/hazard map together with dated training, equipment and site-permission records. Give workers and supervisors a clear route for raising a problem.

Leave unresearched standards and state-plan differences visible as assigned questions. This guide supplies no task-specific standard, incident-reporting deadline or joint-employer ruling. Those require their own evidence rather than a generic safety-complete tick.

seoTitle: Form I-9: hiring deadlines, document checks and retention

sections.heading: Give the hiring entity a practical owner
paragraphs: The employee completes Section 1 at hire. The employer generally examines the required acceptable evidence and completes Section 2 within three business days of hire. For employment lasting less than three business days, the employer’s examination and completion happen at hire instead. These are the separate timing steps in § 274a.2(b)(1).

Those deadlines need someone responsible for the actual hire. An overseas parent should not assume that the local manager, payroll service and group HR team will each understand another party is handling the process. Assign the task, escalation contact and completion evidence before the first employee starts.

The deadline record and the examination procedure answer different questions. Assigning a local person to collect the dates is a practical internal choice; it does not establish that a video call or scan is an authorised examination. Keep the hiring steps separate from the later-of-two-dates retention calculation below.

sections.heading: Do not invent a convenient remote method
paragraphs: The regulation recognises physical examination or an alternative procedure authorised under its specified provision. That does not make every video call, emailed scan or overseas-manager review sufficient. Obtain the current official form and acceptable-document instructions, and check any alternative procedure’s conditions before using it.

The USCIS instruction PDF was inaccessible in the existing review, so its current edition and detailed procedure remain unverified here. That is a concrete outstanding task, not a reason to assume an informal method is acceptable.

sections.heading: Fictional example: calculate both retention dates
paragraphs: An employee is hired on January 15, 2027 and leaves on January 15, 2030. The employer must retain the I-9 for three years after hire or one year after termination, whichever is later (§ 274a.2(b)(2)(i)).

Three years from hire reaches January 15, 2030. One year from departure reaches January 15, 2031, so the later date controls this illustrated I-9 retention calculation. The example is not a live personnel record and does not determine another retention duty. The employer should calculate both dates rather than always deleting a fixed period after departure.

sections.heading: Keep the task log separate from identity documents
paragraphs: The planning log can record the hire date, owner, completion status and retention calculation. Completed forms and identity documents belong in the employer’s controlled personnel system, not this educational site.

Resolve current-form and document-examination questions from official instructions before relying on the process. Individual work authorisation, anti-discrimination, E-Verify and visa-category questions remain separate; a completed planning checklist does not determine them.

learningSummary: The hiring entity needs a Form I-9 process even when its owner stays abroad. The employee and employer have different completion steps and deadlines, and remote ownership does not itself authorise remote document checking. This guide explains the cited regulatory timing and retention framework. The current USCIS form edition and detailed document-examination instructions remain unverified here.

seoTitle: Importer of record: launch equipment, brokers and records

sections.heading: Separate the commercial parties from the customs functions
paragraphs: Identify the seller, purchaser, owner, consignee, proposed importer of record, customs broker and ultimate recipient. One business may perform several roles, but they should be identified rather than assumed.

The importer of record must use reasonable care in providing the relevant entry/completion information. The law’s eligible-filer provisions include the owner or purchaser and an appropriately designated licensed person under the stated conditions. A forwarder’s name on a quote does not establish all those facts or eliminate the need for accurate underlying information (19 U.S. Code § 1484).

sections.heading: Prepare the right-to-enter and product evidence
paragraphs: A party making entry needs evidence of its right to do so through the specified shipping-document arrangements (§ 141.11). Connect those records with the actual commercial invoice, product description, proposed classification, value and origin. Product-agency requirements need separate attention.

The broker can only work from the facts and authority provided. Outsourcing the filing does not replace deciding which party is responsible or providing an accurate account of the shipment. Keep unresolved value, bond, product admissibility and nonresident-importer questions assigned.

sections.heading: Fictional example: demonstration machines at a partner warehouse
paragraphs: An overseas brand sends demonstration machines to a U.S. partner and assumes the warehouse will handle importation. Before dispatch, operations asks who will act as importer, how the broker is authorised, what the machines are worth, how they will be used and whether they will be returned or disposed of.

The warehouse address answers where the goods arrive, not the complete legal arrangement. The resulting role sheet gives the reviewer documents and unresolved questions before the shipment creates avoidable uncertainty. This example does not clear a product or determine a customs value.

A useful question is not simply who will talk to the carrier. It is which party has the relevant entry role and authority, and where the accurate classification, value and origin information will come from. The commercial delivery destination does not answer those questions or establish product admissibility.

Sends demonstration machines.
Who owns or purchases them, their value, use and intended return or disposal.
U.S. partner and warehouse
The machines are to arrive at the partner’s warehouse.
An address or recipient label does not establish the importer-of-record arrangement.
Customs broker
A broker may make filings under the stated conditions.
Identify the actual designation, authority and product facts supplied.
Proposed importer of record
Not established by the shipping quote.
Identify the responsible eligible party and relevant entry/completion information.

sections.heading: Match retention to the record category
paragraphs: Customs records generally have a five-year retention period from entry or the activity creating the record. But the rule contains exceptions, including particular drawback, packing-list, informal-consignee and carrier records (§ 163.4). Do not assign every customs document a five-year deletion date without identifying the category.

Name a document owner for each record and check any other applicable requirement. The general retention rule is a starting point for a category-specific schedule, not a complete product-import checklist.

seoTitle: U.S. import duty estimates: product codes and assumptions

sections.heading: Describe the goods before choosing a code
paragraphs: Record materials, function, composition, dimensions and how the goods are presented at entry. A similar catalogue name can conceal a difference important to the legal classification. Keep any candidate code clearly proposed until the relevant analysis is completed.

Customs entry completion requires classification and rate-of-duty information. USITC’s official help directs users through classification, legal notes, schedule provisions and Customs and Border Protection ruling resources. A commercial calculator does not itself supply a binding classification ruling.

sections.heading: Keep distinct duty questions on distinct lines
paragraphs: Record the schedule version/date, proposed classification, country facts, any claimed preference and each additional-duty or exclusion question. Base duties and additional measures should not disappear into one unexplained percentage.

This guide does not verify a current tariff rate, temporary measure, exclusion, product code or origin preference. That limitation should be visible in the budget. Use a clearly labelled estimate for sensitivity testing while preserving unknown verified-rate cells as unknown.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a scrubber and a replacement battery
paragraphs: A brand plans to import a powered floor scrubber and a replacement battery. Finance puts the whole shipment into “cleaning equipment at 5%.” That line leaves the two products’ classifications and any additional measures untested.

Operations gathers separate specifications and how the items are shipped. The customs reviewer examines the proposed classifications and current provisions for each. Finance can then replace assumptions with supported inputs. The fictional 5% is not an asserted rate for either item and should not be carried into a real shipment model.

Self-check: can the same catalogue category prove both products have the same rate? No. The specifications and applicable provisions must support each answer. The estimate becomes more useful when it distinguishes a known purchase cost, a proposed code, an unverified rate assumption and additional measures still to be checked.

paragraphs: Give the reviewer the product evidence and a rate ledger showing the authority, provision, date, scope, unresolved issue and responsible person. Preserve the reasoning as well as the number.

Revisit landed cost when the product, supplier, production origin or applicable provision changes. Country-of-origin marking, preferential origin and other product admissibility requirements remain separate questions even where they affect the same shipment.

seoTitle: Country-of-origin marking versus brand and tariff origin

sections.heading: Identify which origin question you are answering
paragraphs: Brand ownership, the departure port, marking origin and preferential tariff origin are different facts or legal questions. A Singapore incorporation certificate does not answer where equipment was manufactured or how processing affects its marking origin.

For marking,§ 134.1(b) starts with manufacture, production or growth and addresses further work effecting substantial transformation. It expressly points to Part 102 for relevant NAFTA/USMCA-country marking cases. Preserve that special framework rather than assuming one general transformation rule applies to every product.

sections.heading: Read the general marking rule with its exceptions
paragraphs: Foreign-origin articles, or their containers as applicable, generally must show the English country name conspicuously, legibly, indelibly and with sufficient permanence for the ultimate U.S. purchaser (§ 134.11). Those qualities concern what the recipient can actually see and retain, not just whether a country appears somewhere in paperwork.

The part contains exceptions and special rules. The general wording does not determine whether a particular article, container or downstream operation qualifies for one. Obtain the product-specific answer before assuming a packaging label is enough or that no marking is required.

sections.heading: Fictional example: components and assembly in different countries
paragraphs: A European brand buys components in one country and assembles equipment in another before sending it to the United States. The proposed sticker says “European brand.” That may describe marketing identity but does not establish the manufacturing-origin conclusion.

Operations documents the materials, each production step and the state of the product before and after assembly. The reviewer examines those facts under the relevant marking rules. The example makes no substantial-transformation finding and does not establish a tariff preference or trade-remedy result.

The reviewer needs the product before and after each manufacturing step, not just the names of two countries. The proposed European brand sticker may communicate identity while leaving the required marking question unanswered. Record the marking conclusion separately from preferential tariff origin; this table makes neither finding.

sections.heading: Keep the manufacturing map with the proposed label
paragraphs: Retain a process map, supplier information, proposed artwork and the exact marking question for each product. Link the conclusion to the tariff file, while recognising that the tests can differ.

Review changes to suppliers or production steps before reusing an old conclusion. A label designed for one supply chain should not automatically be copied to goods made through another. Other product-specific labelling requirements still need their own check.

seoTitle: FSVP importer: food, supplier verification and entry data

sections.heading: Name the importer under the food rule
paragraphs: The responsible FSVP importer is the U.S. owner or consignee of the food offered for import. If none exists at entry, the role falls to the U.S. agent or representative of the foreign owner or consignee, with the required signed consent (§ 1.500).

That role can differ from the customs importer, freight forwarder or foreign-facility registration contact. Draw the parties and ask which definition each satisfies. Do not assume that hiring a broker assigns every food and customs responsibility to that business.

sections.heading: A programme depends on the food and supplier
paragraphs: An importer within the rule’s scope generally must develop, maintain and follow a programme for each imported food, subject to the applicable exceptions (§ 1.502). The Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA’s) overview describes qualified individuals, hazard analysis, supplier evaluation, appropriate verification, corrective action and reevaluation.

The needed checks depend on the food and supplier. Do not assume every situation needs the same audit or that one certificate is sufficient. A practical matrix can link each food and foreign supplier to its programme evidence so supplier changes are visible. This does not mean a separate physical document is always legally required for every combination.

sections.heading: Keep exemptions and entry data distinct
paragraphs: Part 1 includes exemptions and modified requirements, including specified U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA)-regulated meat, poultry and egg products outside FSVP. That does not make those foods unrestricted imports. Category and other agency requirements remain separate.

For each line entry, the rule requires the importer’s name, email and FDA-acceptable unique facility identifier and, where relevant, designation before import (§ 1.509). Labelling, prior notice, facility registration and other admissibility duties need their own review.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a branded snack for resale
paragraphs: A training brand proposes sending a packaged snack to its U.S. partner for resale. Before shipment, the supply lead identifies the actual food and producer, the U.S. purchaser at entry, the defined FSVP importer and available programme evidence.

The reviewer assesses category, hazards, supplier and any claimed exemption or modified treatment. The team does not assume a small-sample or small-business exemption from the quantity or company size alone. Its food/party/programme matrix also assigns the separate food-import questions rather than treating the FSVP decision as clearance for the shipment.

Changing the named producer is a fact to bring back to the programme review, not a clerical change to ignore. The matrix links a food and supplier with the applicable evidence without asserting that every pair must have its own separate physical document. Other food-import permissions and any exemption remain to be established.

seoTitle: U.S. trademark clearance: why exact-name searches fall short

sections.heading: Search the actual brand and the actual offer
paragraphs: USPTO guidance recommends a comprehensive search for confusingly similar marks for the same or related goods and services. Sound, spelling, appearance and meaning can matter. A clean exact-name result therefore answers only a narrow search question.

Federal registered and pending records are important, but relevant state records and common-law use can also matter. This guidance recommends a broader investigation; it does not issue legal clearance or determine likelihood of confusion for your proposed mark.

sections.heading: Define the search before interpreting the results
paragraphs: List the word mark, logo, abbreviations, translations and planned goods/services. Search related services and channels rather than only the brand’s existing home-market category. Preserve result identifiers, status, owner, apparent use and date checked.

Distinguish registered or pending records from observed marketplace use. Record similar names even when spelling differs, and leave uncertain first-use dates or geographic limits explicit. A search result needs interpretation; neither a match nor an empty list is a complete rights opinion.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a facilities brand also launches an app
paragraphs: A facilities-services group intends to license its name and a scheduling application in the United States. It has a home-market registration and finds no exact federal match in cleaning services. Management initially treats that as permission to order signage and launch the app.

The clearance brief instead includes the software/service offer, similar marks and related uses. The reviewer assesses the competing rights and gaps before the rollout depends on the name. The example does not conclude that the mark conflicts or can be registered; it explains why the initial search was too narrow.

The entry describes what was searched and what needs interpretation; it is not a fictional clearance certificate. Ordering signage after the first empty result would make the rollout depend on an investigation narrower than the actual U.S. offer. Ownership documents and licence quality controls need their own checks.

sections.heading: Keep a dated brief before licensing the name
paragraphs: The brand owner should retain the search scope, results, unresolved risks and review decision. A partner’s acknowledgement in the licence does not replace investigating the rights the brand proposes to grant.

Registration strategy, ownership-chain evidence and the licence’s quality controls remain separate tasks. Do not present this search workflow as a registration guarantee or a complete licence opinion. The practical output is a transparent record on which a specific rights assessment can be based.

seoTitle: Trade-secret know-how: access controls and immunity notices

sections.heading: Explain both secrecy and value
paragraphs: To qualify as a trade secret, information must be subject to reasonable secrecy measures and have independent economic value from not being generally known or readily ascertainable by proper means (18 U.S. Code § 1839). Document the actual information, why secrecy gives it value and how access is controlled.

Public marketing material does not become a trade secret because a contract labels it so. Lawful independent development and reverse engineering are not automatically misappropriation. The statutory facts and permitted uses need attention alongside the agreement.

sections.heading: Make access and exit practical
paragraphs: Identify which people need which materials, where files are stored, how accounts are issued and revoked, and which copies may be retained. Proportionate access controls should match the information rather than relying only on a broad confidentiality clause.

These controls are business measures relevant to secrecy; they do not establish that every file is legally a secret. Personal information has separate privacy requirements, so restricting access for trade-secret reasons is not a complete cross-border data analysis.

sections.heading: Do not remove protected law-reporting disclosures
paragraphs: The law protects specified confidential disclosures to government officials or an attorney solely to report or investigate suspected legal violations, and sealed court filings under its conditions (§ 1833(b)). Covered employer agreements about trade secrets or confidential information require the immunity notice or a qualifying policy cross-reference.

For this provision, employee includes individual contractors and consultants. The notice rule applies to agreements entered into or updated after May 11, 2016. Missing notice limits the specified exemplary-damages and attorney-fee remedies against the affected employee; it does not automatically void every contract or remove every remedy. Not every company-to-company franchise agreement is a covered employer agreement.

sections.heading: Fictional example: unrestricted manager access
paragraphs: A training business gives a U.S. manager all manuals, customer records and pricing files. The operations lead separates public materials, claimed secrets and personal data, then identifies what the manager actually needs.

The team applies proportionate access and exit controls, checks the recipient agreement and the covered notice question, and assigns the separate privacy review. The result is a know-how/access/exit register, not a ruling that every file is protected or that a particular disclosure is unlawful.

The access decision should follow the actual information and recipient. The immunity notice is a separate agreement question, not proof that every file is a secret. Its absence has the specified exemplary-damages and attorney-fee consequences against the affected employee; it does not automatically void every contract or remove every remedy.

seoTitle: L-1 staff transfers: employment, duties and new-office facts

sections.heading: Keep company, history and duties as separate questions
paragraphs: The regulation generally calls for one continuous year of qualifying full-time employment abroad within the relevant preceding three-year period, alongside the qualifying organisational relationship and role evidence. A licence agreement, supplier relationship or impressive title does not establish those facts.

Record overseas employment dates and actual duties. Brief lawful U.S. trips can receive specific treatment in the continuous-employment calculation; do not automatically count them as foreign employment. The reviewer needs travel facts as well as a start date.

sections.heading: Explain the person’s work and authority
paragraphs: The managerial definition concerns organisation or function management, appropriate authority and discretion. A first-line supervisor is not a manager solely because of supervision, subject to the professional-employee qualification. Executive and specialised-knowledge roles have their own elements.

Use duties, time allocation, reporting lines and supporting staff to explain the proposed job. A small team’s “general manager” may perform several hands-on tasks, so the title alone does not answer the capacity question. No role qualification is decided by this guide.

sections.heading: A new-office plan needs more than incorporation
paragraphs: For a new-office manager/executive, the regulation requires sufficient physical premises and evidence that the intended operation will support the qualifying position within one year of approval, including the proposed organisation and financial ability. Specialised-knowledge new-office provisions differ.

An owner or major stockholder also has specified temporary-service/assignment-abroad evidence under subsection (l)(3)(vii). These are distinct evidence requirements, not a generic minimum-investment promise. Do not transfer one new-office route’s conditions to another without review.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a technical leader becomes the launch manager
paragraphs: A group proposes moving its technical leader to manage a new U.S. office. The initial plan lists only a title and budget. The operations lead adds foreign employment/travel history, actual technical and management duties, staffing, premises and the intended first-year organisation.

The reviewer can now assess the corporate relationship, qualifying capacity and relevant new-office evidence separately. The owner can remain abroad if the independently assessed staffing plan allows; no founder relocation, petition approval or admission is assumed. Keep forms, fees and processing estimates as separate current checks.

A useful first-year sketch explains who will perform the customer work while the proposed manager manages the enterprise or function. It does not need to assume that the founder moves abroad. The applicable new-office route and any owner or major-stockholder evidence still require separate assessment; this sketch does not prove eligibility.

That is a separate requirement from the person’s employment and proposed capacity.

seoTitle: P.L. 86-272: service businesses and state-tax limits

sections.heading: The protected activity has specific conditions
paragraphs: The federal protection concerns state or local net-income tax where the person’s only in-state activities are the specified solicitation of orders for physical goods. The orders must meet the out-of-state approval/rejection and fulfilment conditions in § 381. Those conditions belong together; this is not protection for every interstate transaction.

It does not say that every out-of-state company, website, royalty recipient or service provider is exempt. The statute also excludes specified state-incorporated corporations and resident/domiciled individuals from that protection. Do not read a short summary as broader than the actual provision.

sections.heading: Do not move a goods rule across to every tax and service
paragraphs: Cleaning, consulting, training and managed IT income cannot simply borrow a tangible-goods solicitation protection by analogy. Even where the provision is relevant to goods, a net-income-tax limit does not settle sales/use, payroll, unemployment or gross-receipts taxes, or corporate qualification.

The statute’s defined independent-contractor treatment is also not a general employment-status ruling. Identify what question a term answers in this provision before carrying it into a different area of law.

sections.heading: Fictional example: remote sales and local service delivery
paragraphs: A foreign service brand has no local office but contracts for work performed at U.S. customer sites. Its team writes “no physical office, no tax” and cites P.L.86-272. That conclusion skips both the nature of the activity and the tax type.

The finance lead records who solicits, approves and performs contracts, what is sold, where people work and which entity receives income. The reviewer then examines current rules for each relevant state and tax. The example does not determine a positive tax connection or return obligation in any particular state.

Self-check: if this protection does not answer the service-income question, has the guide proved tax is due? No. The next task is the actual state-by-tax analysis. Failure to establish one protection and a positive filing or liability conclusion are different decisions.

A goods inquiry still needs the provision’s full conditions, exclusions and tax-type limits.

sections.heading: Build a state-by-tax activity register
paragraphs: Use separate rows for income/franchise, sales/use, payroll and local taxes. Record premises, workers, products/services, contracts, solicitation, approval and fulfilment for each entity.

Add a P.L.86-272 question only where its actual goods/activity conditions may matter. Keep formation and qualification records separate from the tax decision. Current thresholds, sourcing, allocation between states and filing requirements require state-specific research; this federal boundary guide is not a 50-state clearance.

seoTitle: Texas IT services: data processing and the 20% exemption

sections.heading: Describe the delivered task rather than the company label
paragraphs: The Comptroller describes entering, storing, manipulating or retrieving a customer’s data as data processing, while merely using a computer to perform a professional service is different. Its examples contrast data work with engineering or bookkeeping judgement and interpretation.

The labels IT, consulting and B 2 B do not classify every invoice line. List the actual deliverables, the customer data involved and the judgement or interpretation supplied. A hosting/storage task and an advisory task may raise different questions even when sold by the same team.

sections.heading: Read the 20% provision as an exemption of value
paragraphs: Texas Tax Code§ 151.0035 defines data processing with exclusions, and§ 151.0101(a)(12) includes it among taxable services. Section 151.351 exempts 20 percent of the value of information services and data processing services. That is not a 20% tax rate or a blanket exemption for IT contracts.

For illustration, if$1,000 is otherwise-taxable qualifying data-processing value, the stated exemption removes $200, leaving $800 before any other applicable adjustments. The actual tax amount still depends on the applicable rates and other facts. The calculation does not determine this contract’s category, sourcing or seller obligations.

sections.heading: Fictional example: data work and advice on one contract
paragraphs: A service business proposes one contract covering data entry, storage and interpretation of results. Renaming the whole invoice consulting does not explain the actual work. Finance separates the deliverables, proposed charges and evidence of customer use.

The Comptroller publication addresses distinct/identifiable nontaxable services, reasonable separate charges and documentation for mixed bundles. It also addresses use inside and outside Texas. The reviewer needs those facts before determining treatment; a new invoice heading is not a substitute for them.

The earlier $1,000 example answers only how the stated 20% value exemption works after qualifying otherwise-taxable value has been identified: $200 is removed and $800 remains before other adjustments. It does not classify these fictional mixed deliverables, establish a final rate or decide whether this seller must register and collect.

What the customer receives and evidence of its use.

Interpretation or advice
Describe the staff judgement supplied and the proposed charge.
Determine whether a distinct identifiable nontaxable service and reasonable separate charge are supported.

sections.heading: Create a service-line tax schedule
paragraphs: For each deliverable, record the data activity, staff judgement, price evidence, location/use and unresolved classification. Keep the confidential contract and any multistate-use certificates in the authorised accounting process, outside this site.

Separate service classification, exemption/base calculation, seller tax connection or registration, sourcing and final rate. The statutory review is limited to the named Texas sections and the Comptroller guidance is revision 03/2022. Other states and later amendments to their service categories need separate work.

seoTitle: U.S.–UK royalty treaty benefits: ownership and LOB evidence

sections.heading: Keep the four entitlement questions distinct
paragraphs: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) guidance identifies relevant residence, beneficial ownership, derivation of income and applicable LOB conditions for reduced treaty withholding. A form or treaty-country mailing address does not replace the underlying entitlement evidence. The payer must consider actual knowledge or reason to know of ineligibility.

Finance should therefore identify the actual recipient and income before placing a treaty rate in the cash model. A change in payee or ownership may change the questions even if the brand and bank account name look familiar.

sections.heading: Read the UK articles and protocol together
paragraphs: Article 4 defines residence. Article 12 addresses royalties with permanent-establishment, special-relationship and conduit conditions. Article 23 contains multiple eligibility routes and limitations. For example, Article 23(2)(f)’s ownership/base-erosion route has both ownership-period and deductible-payment conditions. UK incorporation alone is not that test.

The July 2002 protocol replaces Article 23(7)(d). Do not rely on the unamended equivalent-beneficiary wording in the 2001 PDF. This guide does not resolve a derivative-benefits or post-Brexit question; it identifies the need to use the amended text and applicable route.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the new UK receiving company
paragraphs: A group proposes paying U.S. royalties to a UK company and assumes its registration proves treaty eligibility. The preparer asks instead who owns it during the relevant period, how the income is treated, who beneficially owns it, what deductible payments leave the company and which LOB paragraph is relied on.

Those facts can be assembled without choosing a favourable result. The reviewer checks residence, the royalty article and the selected amended eligibility route separately. The example quotes no treaty rate and does not decide the company’s entitlement.

For each row, record a document custodian and the unresolved fact instead of entering treaty eligible on the strength of incorporation. The schedule does not choose an LOB route, resolve derivative benefits or post-Brexit treatment, or supply a royalty rate. It also cannot be reused as an E-2 nationality decision.

sections.heading: Produce an article-by-article evidence schedule
paragraphs: For each claimed condition, record the source paragraph, period, evidence custodian and unresolved fact. Link any withholding certificate to the actual recipient and income. Keep the treaty assumption unknown in the cash model until supported.

Tax residence and beneficial ownership are also different from the E-2 enterprise-nationality inquiry. Do not reuse an immigration ownership diagram as a complete treaty file, or copy a UK eligibility path to another country’s treaty.

seoTitle: Trademark quality control versus franchise operating control

sections.heading: The trademark provisions concern marked goods and services
paragraphs: The trademark definition of a related company concerns the owner’s control over the nature and quality of the marked goods or services (§ 1127). Another provision addresses legitimate related-company use and controlled first use benefiting the registrant/applicant, with a condition against public deception (§ 1055).

These provisions make the actual quality system important. They do not dictate or approve any particular staffing rule, software requirement or inspection programme. A complete licence-validity or abandonment opinion would also require the applicable law and cases beyond this statutory distinction.

sections.heading: The franchise inquiry asks a different question
paragraphs: The FTC framework separately examines brand association, significant operating control or assistance, and required payment. Calling a provision trademark protection does not decide its practical effect.

Separate artwork approval from requirements about scheduling, staffing, sales methods or mandatory systems. A control can have mixed purposes. Record both rather than forcing it into one category to obtain a preferred legal label. The May 2008 FTC guide provides explanatory context, read with the current rule.

sections.heading: Fictional example: logo approval and a scheduling system
paragraphs: A brand requires approval of vehicle logos and also dictates job acceptance, staff allocation and customer scheduling through mandatory software. The operations lead explains the quality outcome protected by each requirement and how defects are checked and corrected.

The reviewer can then examine trademark use and the wider operating relationship separately. Deleting every check to avoid one test may leave an unanswered trademark question; adding detailed management controls may create franchise questions. The example does not declare either document valid or the arrangement a franchise.

The comparison does not declare logo approval legally sufficient or software automatically decisive. Trademark use and the complete franchise relationship need their respective analyses. Removing every check is not the lesson; explaining what each check actually does is.

sections.heading: Keep both preparation records
paragraphs: One file identifies the owner, authorised user, quality standards, inspections and corrections for marked goods/services. The second explains the complete business relationship for federal and independent state franchise analysis.

For every control, name the quality attribute, business effect, person checking it and correction process. Route the unanswered questions to the relevant reviewer. This practical table helps reveal mixed purposes; it is not a statutory safe harbour or a complete survey of uncontrolled-licensing case law.

seoTitle: Sanctions screening: name matches, ownership and transactions

sections.heading: A similarity score is not transaction clearance
paragraphs: Commerce says apparent CSL matches need additional due diligence and confirmation against the official source list. A fuzzy-name score measures similarity, not the probability that a deal is lawful.

Record names, aliases, appropriate identifiers, addresses, source list and search date. Explain why an apparent match is or is not the actual party. Do not treat all lists alike: identify the restriction associated with the particular source and person before deciding the consequence.

sections.heading: Ownership can affect an entity not separately listed
paragraphs: OFAC FAQ 401 explains direct/indirect ownership and aggregation under the 50 Percent Rule. Its examples show why simply multiplying every percentage can mislead. If a blocked person owns 50% of Entity A, A is blocked; A’s 50% ownership of Entity B can in turn make B blocked.

A search for Entity B’s name alone could miss that result. Trace the chain and apply the actual ownership rule rather than assuming a missing name means no restriction. Equally, do not replace the prescribed analysis with an informal control test.

The point is the order of analysis, not a mathematical prediction about every ownership chain. Establish the relevant blocked owners and apply the actual direct, indirect and aggregation rules. Control below 50% remains subject to the separate qualifications explained below, rather than becoming universal permission.

paragraphs: FAQ 398 says control without 50% aggregate ownership is not automatic blocking under this ownership rule, but warns about other designation/blocking criteria and dealings involving a blocked representative. Below 50% is therefore not universal permission.

Party screening also does not settle goods or technology, destination, end-use, country-programme or authorisation requirements. A country connection is not always a blanket ban, just as a clean name result is not a complete export decision.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a prospective distribution partner
paragraphs: A brand considers a distributor whose name produces no apparent match. The team records the result but also obtains the relevant ownership chain and the proposed goods, destination and use. It assigns any unresolved source-list and transaction questions before payment, access or shipment depends on clearance.

The screening register should identify the reviewer and source-specific result, then be revisited when parties, ownership, goods or restrictions change. This site performs no live search and does not certify a partner as clean.

seoTitle: Franchise network pricing: vertical and competitor issues

sections.heading: Understand what Leegin actually decided
paragraphs: In Leegin Creative Leather Products v. PSKS, 551 U.S. 877 (2007), the Supreme Court majority overruled the prior Dr. Miles federal per-se treatment of vertical minimum resale-price agreements and required rule-of-reason analysis. The Court reversed and remanded—sent the case back for further proceedings.

That outcome is not a finding that every policy, or the particular arrangement, was lawful. The cited record supplies the 2007 majority’s standard and disposition, not an independently checked later merits outcome. Current FTC guidance also explains that state-law treatment can differ.

sections.heading: Map who competes and who makes the decision
paragraphs: FTC guidance distinguishes manufacturer/dealer restrictions, unilateral policy decisions and competitor coordination. A network can contain several relationships, especially where the brand also operates units.

Record whether operators coordinate or collectively pressure the brand. Calling an arrangement vertical does not settle horizontal effects. State and international minimum-price rules may also differ from the federal framework. MAP, MFN, territory and customer restrictions require their own actual terms to be examined.

sections.heading: Fictional example: operators ask for a common price
paragraphs: Several independent service operators ask the brand to establish a common network price. The brand also has its own operating unit. Rather than assuming the request is an ordinary brand standard, the team preserves who proposed it, the communications, competitive relationships and intended enforcement.

The reviewer can then distinguish suggested from required prices, unilateral decisions from agreement, and the claimed service/quality purpose from effects on competition. The example clears no price policy or customer allocation and makes no finding about the fictional parties.

Self-check: did Leegin approve this fictional common-price proposal? No. It changed the specified federal standard of review and remanded that case. This proposal still needs assessment under the actual party relationships, competitive facts and relevant state or international rules.

The rule-of-reason standard does not itself establish that the arrangement is lawful.

sections.heading: Prepare the policy before announcing it
paragraphs: Keep the proposed rule, discounts, advertising support, territories, reserved customers and methods used to induce compliance. Preserve communications and evidence supporting any claimed service investment.

Build a policy/party/effects file with separate federal, state and international questions. The standard of review tells the reviewer what must be examined; it is not a badge of legality to place beside a standard price list.

seoTitle: Worker classification: wage, investigation and tax tests

sections.heading: Understand why the source dates look inconsistent
paragraphs: In the existing November 12, 2026 review, current 29 CFR Part 795 still contains the 2024 economic-reality interpretation. It examines the whole activity with six nonexclusive factors; no single factor or chosen subset necessarily decides the result.

The Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division issued a May 1, 2025 bulletin telling investigators to use a different approach within its stated scope and discretion. It expressly says it does not change employees’ rights or employers’ responsibilities. A February 27, 2026 proposed rule seeks rescission/replacement and proposed expansion to the Family and Medical Leave Act and the Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act. Those source types must not be treated as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Collect business facts rather than scoring labels
paragraphs: Record who sets prices and schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, makes entrepreneurial investments, markets to other customers and bears a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. Include actual practice and reserved rights.

Under the codified interpretation, specialised skill alone does not establish an independent business. A licence, contract label or remote location does not settle status either. Do not turn a multifactor inquiry into a points tally. Explain the circumstances and missing evidence so the governing test can be applied.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the “independent” technician
paragraphs: A maintenance brand’s agreement calls a technician an independent contractor. The operations file shows mandatory schedules, brand-set prices and the technician’s equipment purchases, but says little about outside customers, hiring helpers or opportunity for profit and loss.

The team gathers those missing facts instead of announcing a result from either the label or one investment. It then identifies the current governing wage-law, tax and relevant state tests. This example classifies no worker; it shows how to produce a file useful under more than one inquiry.

The same fact file can support several reviews without making their legal tests identical. The codified interpretation examines the whole activity with six nonexclusive factors; IRS evidence has its own organisation. The unreconciled opinion references and unverified latest appellate developments described below remain unresolved, not assumptions in a current-status answer.

paragraphs: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) employment-tax guidance groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. It examines the whole relationship rather than a magic number of factors; a right to control can matter for remote workers.
A payroll-tax decision or relief provision is not a universal answer under the FLSA or state unemployment/wage law. Give each test its own authority, date, unresolved question and responsible person.

sections.heading: Read the court example within its limits
paragraphs: The January 9, 2025 Colt & Joe Trucking opinion/order found the challenger lacked standing and explained that its arguments would otherwise fail or were waived. It did not classify every driver or service technician. The February 2026 proposal reports appeals/stays as of its publication; the latest appellate dockets were not independently checked.

The bulletin and proposal also cite different associated opinion numbers; this guide does not reconcile or apply those opinions. Keep dated case reporting distinct from a current judicial-status assertion. The practical output is one worker-facts file plus a separate test/status register before relying on contractor treatment.

Begin with the person’s real business activity and identify which test and source status apply. The recorded opinion-reference discrepancy and latest appellate status remain unresolved, so this page supplies no universal current classification result.

seoTitle: Joint employers: separate NLRA control and FLSA duties

sections.heading: The current NLRA rule was restored through final action
paragraphs: The National Labor Relations Board’s (NLRB’s) February 27, 2026 final action states that the 2023 rule never took effect after district-court vacatur and restores the 2020 text immediately. Current§ 103.40 matches that action. Substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role.

This is the NLRA framework, not a rule for every employment statute. Do not convert its treatment of one kind of control into a general conclusion that all brand standards are safe or that a brand can never be an employer.

sections.heading: Keep the court step and the wage-law position clear
paragraphs: The Chamber of Commerce v. NLRB opinion/order was ordered March 8, 2024 and filed March 18 as Document 47. Its remedy discussion states that final judgment will vacate the 2023 replacement and removal of the earlier text. The 2026 final rule independently confirms the resulting regulatory action. The cited court document is not a complete current docket search.

For the FLSA, current Part 791 is reserved. That does not mean joint-employer liability disappeared. DOL’s April 23, 2026 publication is a proposal, not an effective rule or franchise safe harbour. Governing court law and actual employment facts remain relevant; the NLRA history does not answer them.

sections.heading: A real agency example: one worker, two businesses
paragraphs: DOL Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 addresses a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those supplied facts, DOL concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for FLSA compliance.

The lesson is that separate incorporation or payroll systems did not answer that inquiry on those facts. The letter expressly limits its view to the information supplied. It is not a court judgment about every franchise or every pair of related businesses.

sections.heading: Build a control-and-hours map
paragraphs: For each entity, record who selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, directs performance, disciplines and terminates. Keep service/brand standards and employment decisions in separate columns, including mixed-purpose controls.

For example, an inspection of the contracted service outcome and a direct instruction about a named worker’s shift should be recorded accurately rather than both labelled quality control. Neither fact alone decides the complete test. Add shared-worker hours, managers and actual practice so the reviewer can assess the NLRA, FLSA and relevant state questions separately.

This comparison identifies facts rather than a safe list of brand controls. The agency letter above supplies a bounded example where hours were combined on the represented facts; it does not decide this fictional relationship. A full governing-court or state-law answer is not supplied by this guide.

Record the purpose and actual conduct; do not label every check an employment decision.

Record each entity’s hours and actual operations.
